brief.text:
GANGSTAS PARADISE (Sleeper) — FINAL WEEK 1: LOST 118.06-151.56 to AdufortheWin84; Zay Flowers exited with a re-aggravated hamstring, MRI pending, Week 2 watch
Do now: nothing to set today — no games until Thursday's Week 2 slate. Watch for Flowers' MRI result before next lineup lock.
Locks next 24h: none
Lineup: Week 1 is fully banked, no changes possible. Chase Brown (18.8), Strange (10.3), Tuten (9.8) and the Jaguars D (15.0) all delivered as projected in a 34-10 JAX rout of Cleveland. Flowers went off for 26.0 (150 yds, 1 TD) in a 41-23 win over Indianapolis before leaving with a hamstring injury — not considered long-term per Ian Rapoport, but a real Week 2 question. Herbert (14.26) and Hampton (8.3) were the week's bust, LAC fell 26-14 at Arizona despite the plus matchup on paper. If Flowers can't go Week 2 vs New Orleans, Stefon Diggs is the direct bench replacement — he's still rostered for exactly this.

GAME OF THROWS (Yahoo) — Isaiah Likely goes off for 2 TDs in a 28-20 Giants win over Dallas; final Yahoo score still unconfirmed — send a fresh screenshot
Do now: drop a Week 1 final-score screenshot (Players > Matchup) into the War room Drive folder — the newest file there is still Sunday morning pre-kickoff, same batch as last run, so I can't confirm your actual Week 1 result or final bench points
Locks next 24h: none
Lineup: real-world results only, since I have no fresh box score — Chase Brown and the Bengals beat Tampa 33-27, Garrett Wilson and the Jets beat Tennessee 23-10 in his first game back since November, Parker Washington and Jacksonville routed Cleveland 34-10, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns were the ones getting routed (toughest matchup of the week lived down to it), Travis Etienne and the Saints lost a 31-30 shootout at Detroit with Kamara inactive the whole game, George Pickens and Dallas fell 28-20 at NYG on Sunday Night, and Isaiah Likely turned in the roster's best game — 2 TD catches from Jaxson Dart, with Malik Nabers active and looking comfortable in his return from ACL surgery. Stafford, Myers and the 49ers were already banked from Wed/Thu.

FYI: Chase Brown starts in both leagues and cashed in on the Bengals' 33-27 win; the Jacksonville stack (Strange, Tuten, JAX DEF in Sleeper; Parker Washington in Yahoo) had a monster week behind the 34-10 blowout of Cleveland, whose Judkins sat on the other side of that same score in Yahoo.
Data: Sleeper live (Week 1 final) · Yahoo screenshots still from 2026-09-13 pre-kickoff (same images used in Sunday's run) — send a fresh one showing your final Week 1 score.

waivers.text:
SLEEPER — TE is still the priority: you roster zero backup there, and Strange shares Week 7's JAX/LAC bye cluster with Herbert, Hampton, Tuten, and your DEF. FAAB budget is untouched at $100 (nobody in the league has spent a dollar yet) and you sit waiver position 3.
1. Darren Waller (TE, CAR) — Carolina's TE2 on the depth chart behind Tommy Tremble but the far more proven player with real path to the job. Drop Fernando Mendoza (your QB3, confirmed as Vegas' backup behind Kirk Cousins — zero standalone value). FAAB $9.
2. Samaje Perine (RB, CIN) — the direct backup to Chase Brown, who anchors your RB1 slot in BOTH leagues; this is bye-week and injury insurance you don't currently have anywhere on either roster. Drop Zachariah Branch (WR, no role in ATL). FAAB $7.
3. Justice Hill (RB, BAL) — locked in as Derrick Henry's clear #2 and the passing-down back in a full-PPR league; real standalone flex value. Drop Zavion Thomas (WR, no role in CHI). FAAB $6.
4. AJ Barner (TE, SEA) — second TE flier if you miss on Waller or want a true pair. Drop Michael Wilson (WR, buried behind Marvin Harrison Jr./Trey McBride in the ARI target mix, no path to a role). FAAB $4.
5. Roschon Johnson (RB, CHI) — cheap speculative stash in a muddled Bears backfield. Only add if you're willing to also cut Woody Marks or Stefon Diggs — your 6 bench spots are full once picks 1-4 land. FAAB $3.
No DEF/K stream needed this week — Aubrey and the Jaguars D&ST both carry plus Week 1 matchups per the Analysis tab.

YAHOO — still no access to the Yahoo free-agent pool this run (private league, no login, screenshots only). Isaiah Likely being confirmed healthy lowers urgency at TE, but Chig Okonkwo remains a thin TE2 if you want a stopgap plan. Drop a fresh screenshot of the free-agent list (Players > Available, filtered by position) into the War room Drive folder and next run can give you real availability and bid guidance.

trades.text:
SLEEPER — send Stefon Diggs to Grandmasterfabe ("Master Bate$ LaPortapotty") for Jake Ferguson (TE, DAL). Diggs is stuck behind Higgins, Flowers, and Downs on your bench with no path to starting reps; Grandmasterfabe is stacked at WR (Olave, DeVonta Smith, Jameson Williams, Jakobi Meyers, Alec Pierce) but is rolling with rookie Harold Fannin as their only real TE, with Ferguson buried as insurance. Diggs gives them a proven bye-week/injury-fill starter; you turn a fully blocked bench piece into the backup TE you currently have nowhere on the roster, which matters with Strange sharing the Week 7 JAX/LAC bye cluster. It's a mild overpay in raw value on your side, justified by how scarce TE depth is around this league right now — nobody scanned so far is sitting on two startable options. Checked your Weeks 15-17 outlook first: Diggs isn't projected to be a playoff starter behind your current WR corps, so moving him costs you nothing down the stretch.

YAHOO — no trade idea this run. I don't have visibility into other managers' rosters or trade blocks in your private Yahoo league (screenshots only cover your team and this week's opponent), so I can't responsibly name a real deal. No trade.txt found in the War room folder either.

news.headline: Zay Flowers exits with hamstring injury
news.summary: Flowers piled up 150 yards and a touchdown on 5 catches before re-aggravating a hamstring injury late in the first half against Indianapolis and was ruled out for the rest of Week 1; Ian Rapoport reported the injury isn't considered long-term, but an MRI will determine the Week 2 timeline against New Orleans.

news.headline: Takeaways as Giants outplay Cowboys 28-20 on Sunday Night Football
news.summary: Likely caught two touchdown passes from Jaxson Dart as the Giants opened John Harbaugh's tenure with a 28-20 win over Dallas, the best game of the week for either of this roster's tight ends.

news.headline: Sunday Night Football Inactives: WR Malik Nabers is active for Giants vs. Cowboys
news.summary: Nabers was ultimately active and played in his return from last year's torn ACL, with the final call left up to his own comfort level; the Giants won 28-20, and his availability keeps Likely's role from being the lone read in that offense going forward.
